correctness.rationale: The source supplies the exact independent radial-angular representation and beta law for the radius. The p-generalized-normal representation makes the powered angular coordinates Dirichlet. For one observation, the event that the support-boundary root lies within t of p is exactly a beta upper-tail event with an angular threshold. Its threshold has first-order coefficient H(W)/p and a dimension-uniform bound from the power-sum inequality, so dominated convergence gives the exact tail constant. The iid maximum then yields almost-sure consistency and the Weibull limit at rate M^{-p/(p-d+1)}. All boundary cases excluded from the theorem are stated explicitly.

value.rationale: The direct source explicitly proposes p-star as a natural estimator because the ordinary likelihood may fail to attain a maximum, but gives no performance theory. The finding supplies the missing consistency, exact nonregular rate, full limiting law, and model-specific scale constant in every dimension and every finite p>d-1. The rate changes continuously from extremely fast near the singular boundary p=d-1 toward an M^{-1} endpoint rate, making the result useful for interpreting and calibrating the estimator rather than being a routine algebraic corollary.
